# Summary {#part-foundations-summary .unnumbered}

The first substantive part followed the model before it becomes a product: how scale is budgeted, how data is selected, how bytes become tokens, how Transformer variants arrange computation, and how a training run survives the cluster. The mid-training chapter then showed that the path from broad pretraining to post-training is no longer a blank space; it is where quality, domain mixture, specialization, and context length are adjusted before behavior is explicitly shaped.

The concern running through the part is irreversibility. Data mixture, vocabulary, architecture, precision, parallelism, and continuation curriculum all look like preparation, but they become inherited constraints. Later serving, adaptation, evaluation, and safety work can compensate for some of those choices, yet it cannot freely rewrite them.

The practical takeaway is that pretraining is infrastructure, not background. The open question is how much room remains for scaling once natural corpora thin out and hardware economics tighten. Higher-quality data, synthetic data, and mid-training may stretch the curve, but the part leaves that as a constraint to be tested rather than a promise to assume.
